To prevent data leakage and ensure robust model testing, the models were trained on only two of these ATs and the third was reserved for testing. Furthermore, the training and testing data were split temporally, using the first 80% of data for model training and the remaining 20% for testing. This approach ensured that the model was tested on both a different AT and a distinct timeframe compared to the training data. To enhance the robustness of this evaluation, a second test was conducted on a completely different AT, entirely separate from those used for initial training and testing. Importantly, the data for this second test was sourced from April 2024, providing an independent dataset for model assessment. A variety of DDMs were developed to forecast err . These included a simple average model, mech a multivariate linear regression model, two eXtreme Gradient (XG) Boosted models, and two long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network (NN) models.
